source: NASA/JPL Horizons API, spacecraft ephemerides; Earth-Moon rotating frame, scaled to 384400 km

missions.name: Artemis I
missions.what: Uncrewed Orion test flight launched on the SLS rocket. It flew past the Moon, entered a distant retrograde orbit and returned to Earth.

missions.name: Artemis II
missions.what: Crewed Orion flight around the Moon and back.

missions.name: CAPSTONE
missions.what: Small satellite that tested the near-rectilinear halo orbit planned for the Gateway station, reached by a low-energy transfer.

missions.name: Danuri (KPLO)
missions.what: South Korea's first lunar orbiter, sent on a low-energy ballistic transfer of about four and a half months.

missions.name: SLIM
missions.what: Japan's Smart Lander for Investigating Moon: a long, fuel-saving transfer, lunar orbit, then a precision landing in January 2024.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-3 lander
missions.what: India's lander. Several Earth-orbit raising burns, trans-lunar injection, then the landing near the south pole on 23 August 2023.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-2 lander
missions.what: India's Vikram lander, which came down hard during its landing attempt on 6 September 2019.

missions.name: LADEE
missions.what: Lunar Atmosphere and Dust Environment Explorer, an orbiter that studied the thin lunar exosphere.

missions.name: Apollo 8 rocket stage
missions.what: The Saturn V third stage (S-IVB) after it sent Apollo 8 toward the Moon. Horizons holds the stage, not the capsule.

missions.name: Apollo 10 rocket stage
missions.what: The Saturn V third stage (S-IVB) after it sent Apollo 10 toward the Moon.

missions.name: Apollo 11 rocket stage
missions.what: The Saturn V third stage (S-IVB) after it sent Apollo 11 toward the Moon. The crew left it behind, so this is the outbound leg only.

missions.name: Apollo 12 rocket stage
missions.what: The Saturn V third stage (S-IVB) after it sent Apollo 12 toward the Moon.
